newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks Canada's help to extradite Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks Canada's help to extradite Pol Pot.

text.p: The United States has asked Canada to help extradite Khmer Rouge guerrilla chief Pol Pot from Cambodia so he can be tried by an international tribunal for crimes against humanity, the New York Times reports.

In Monday's edition, the Times, quoting unnamed American and foreign officials, said U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright asked Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy to request the extradition under Canada's law against genocide.
Only Canada and Denmark have such laws permitting them to make such a request, the Times said.
If Canada agrees, the United States is ready to coordinate sending a military team to Cambodia to remove Pol Pot, the Times said.

As part of a plan being worked out, Pol Pot would be extradited to Canada as a temporary measure until an international tribunal could be convened to try him under the international Genocide Convention.
More than one million people were executed as enemies of Pol Pot's utopian revolution or died of disease, starvation or overwork during the Khmer Rouge's 1975-79 rule.

Cambodia's first prime minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh insisted on Monday that Pol Pot was alive, and a senior military officer said he was being held in the jungle village headquarters of a breakaway Khmer Rouge faction and would be transferred to Phom Penh.
